items: Suffix appended to nominal stems to create a masculine noun, usually denoting a professional, performer, adherent, place, object, tool or a feature. — лы́жа (“ski”) + -ник → лы́жник (“skier”); путь (“way, path, road”) + -ник → пу́тник (“traveler”); бюдже́т (“budget”) + -ник → бюдже́тник (“government employee”)

blocks.text: The suffix has the same properties as -ный:
A velar (as well as ц) normally turns into a palatal as a result of the Slavic first palatalization.
A stem ending in -л turns into -ль before the suffix; contrariwise, all other stems ending in -ь lose this.

items: -er, -an, -ian (nominal suffix for agent nouns or nouns designating persons). — Аме́рика (“America”) + -е́ц → америка́нец (“American”); боро́ться (“to fight, wrestle”) + -ец → боре́ц (“champion, wrestler”); вдова́ (“widow”) + -ец → вдове́ц (“widower”)
Diminutive suffix. — зуб (“tooth”) + -ец → зубе́ц (“cog”); столб (“pole”) + -ец → столбе́ц (“column”); суп (“soup”) + -ец → супе́ц (“soup (diminutive)”)
Suffix added to nouns, verbs and sometimes adjectives to form masculine agent nouns: -er, -or — вре́мя (“time; (obsolete) fortunate incident”) + -щик → временщи́к (“(historical) minion”)

blocks.text: Triggers the first Slavic palatalisation and palatalisation of stem-final /л/.
After coronal obstruents this suffix is written -чик. Stem-final /ч/ is written т.
